summary.intent: Manage CipherBox milestone v2.0 via the GSD manager: verify/plan/execute/ship remaining phases (69–79), and specifically root-cause and fix a persistent macOS-only Desktop-E2E test failure on PR #607 rather than deferring or dismissing it as infra flakiness.
summary.outcome: Phases 69, 70.1, 75, and 77 were completed and verified; Phase 74 was shipped to PR #607 after finding and fixing several real defects (SC#2 hex/base64 encoding bug, dirty-resume revocation-bypass gap, Greptile P1 WinFsp kind-mismatch, and a deep macOS FUSE-T rotation race). A new access-token TTL issue surfaced during the fix-verification CI run and was mid-fix when the session ended; PR #607 remains unmerged awaiting final green CI.

repo: Two incompatible wire encodings coexist with no type-level enforcement: internal node-codec fields (readKeySealed, read_sealed) use base64, but ALL share API DTOs (create-share, create-invite, claim-invite, update-grant) validate encryptedReadKey/encryptedWriteKey/itemNameEncrypted as hex via @Matches regex — this has caused repeated bugs and only surfaces at the real API boundary (unit tests mock past it).

macOS FUSE-T/SMB's overwrite-rename calls open() on the SOURCE file; Linux's kernel rename never opens either file. This is the reason identical rotation/test code passes on Linux/Windows but fails deterministically on macOS.

GSD's plan-scan.cjs (line 28) has a loose /PLAN/i substring fallback that miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' as a plan file (e.g. '...WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md'), causing false 'partial'/'Executing' dashboard status on fully complete phases.

Sub-agents launched at the repo root cannot EnterWorktree into a pre-existing worktree — this makes parallel worktree-isolated background planning agents unable to finish their own pipeline reliably; sequential main-checkout-on-feat-branch processing is the working alternative.

FUSE-T vs macFUSE linking is ambiguous via default pkg-config on this machine (fuse.pc resolves to macFUSE); building against real FUSE-T (as CI does) requires a PKG_CONFIG_PATH override with an aliased fuse-t.pc.
vitest ignores .env — SDK_E2E_SECRET must be exported inline into the shell running the suite, not just present in apps/api/.env.

Access-token TTL is hardcoded to 15m in apps/api/src/auth/services/token.service.ts; the headless desktop e2e binary authenticates once at startup with no refresh-on-401, so long-running suites (especially the slow macOS leg with its sync-wait steps) exceed the TTL and 401 mid-run.

fs.rs's drain_refresh_completions already guards mutated_folders/publish_queue from being clobbered by stale metadata refreshes (falls back to mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved which preserves keys) — but scope-exit rotation republishes folders out-of-band via the rotation engine and never populated that set, so the guard didn't apply to rotated folders.

code.finding: The actual shipped fix: after rotate_read_on_scope_exit refreshes inode keys, the rotated folders (grant root + all folders in result.rotated_nodes) are now inserted into fs.mutated_folders, leveraging the existing drain_refresh_completions guard to prevent a stale in-flight metadata refresh from clobbering the freshly-rotated read keys.

Rotation republishes nodes with write_sealed:None — write-plane preservation was deferred to a Phase-72 follow-up; a prototyped fix (reconstructing write_sealed from the mount's in-memory write plane) worked (607→0 'no write_sealed body' errors) but was reverted as orthogonal to the Part D failure and filed as a separate todo.

Grant re-mint encoded encryptedReadKey as base64 via base64_encode(&wrapped), but the share-grant API wire field requires hex — causing a real runtime 400 on live FUSE→API round-trips that all mocked unit tests missed. Fixed to hex::encode.

WinFsp handle_rename only guarded against non-empty-folder overwrite, missing the kind-mismatch guard (file↔directory) that crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/rename.rs:105-122 already has for the fuser path — a real Greptile P1 security parity gap, fixed by porting the guard with new NTSTATUS helpers.

Access-token TTL hardcoded to 15m; being made env-configurable (ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL) with production default preserved, to support long single-session desktop-e2e runs on macOS that exceed 15 minutes due to slow sync-wait test steps.

Async FilePointer resolution captures the file's read_key at spawn time; a concurrent rotation can invalidate that captured key mid-flight. A read-path self-heal (re-resolve with current inode key) was tried and proven insufficient — the published data itself, not just the captured key, could be inconsistent when the parent's stale republish reverted the child-ref.

workflow: When a user insists a CI failure is real and reproducible (not flaky/infra), reproduce it locally end-to-end before theorizing — building against the actual platform toolchain (FUSE-T, not macFUSE) was essential to get a faithful repro.

Iteratively instrumenting each layer with targeted debug logging (key fingerprints at publish/childref/unseal points) and testing one hypothesis at a time, reverting each failed attempt to keep the diff minimal, was what eventually pinpointed the true root cause after four wrong hypotheses.

Don't hand-wave a CI failure as an 'infra flake' without evidence — the user corrected this twice in the session, both times revealing a real, previously undiagnosed bug (the 401 mischaracterization masked... nothing new; but the FUSE-T rotation race was real and the correction was warranted).

Confirm a resolve/consistency hypothesis with direct instrumentation before touching a crypto/resolve seam — the user's explicit choice to 'confirm resolve, then fix API' avoided a wasted/wrong API-side fix.

Cron-based autonomous resume (CronCreate/CronDelete) across quota-window resets, with corrected recovery instructions each time a prior approach (worktree EnterWorktree) was found to be a dead end, kept a multi-hour background campaign progressing without user babysitting.

friction: Session quota limits interrupted work repeatedly (mid-planning, mid-execution, mid-CI-monitoring), requiring cron-based scheduled resumes with progressively corrected instructions.
Background planning agents using EnterWorktree into pre-existing worktrees failed uniformly — a full dead-end that required pivoting strategy and re-committing in-flight draft work.
Assistant twice mischaracterized real bugs as 'infra flakes' (401 auth noise, macOS 'flake') before the user pushed back with direct evidence, requiring a redo of the diagnosis.

Four wrong-root-cause hypotheses (write_sealed preservation, FilePointer self-heal, coalesced dest-gate exclusion, API resolve lag) were implemented, locally tested, and reverted before the real cause (stale refresh clobbering rotated keys) was found — ~10 build+test iterations, each ~10 minutes.
gsd commit helper occasionally false-negatives 'commit_failed' while the commit actually lands, requiring manual git log verification instead of blind retries.
FUSE-T vs macFUSE library linking ambiguity on the local macOS dev machine required a non-obvious PKG_CONFIG_PATH workaround to get a faithful CI-equivalent build.
